text:
All five landed in 61590dc. Each is named for its relation, with worked cases from two kinds of work and the arithmetic in each case's worked field. Each was checked by skills.py check and run-cases, and the library index now holds 29 skills.
(1) standard_error_of_independent_estimates@v1 (data_analysis): mean, sample standard deviation over n - 1, and standard error s/sqrt(n) of independent estimates (per block, subset or replicate). Cases: D per block of a Brownian run; a peak position per subset of a spectrometer's scans. Source: Grossfield et al., LiveCoMS 2018, Eqs. 6 and 8, read verbatim; its block-averaging section came to me through a summary only, and the manifest's note says so.
(2) power_law_exponent_along_sweep@v1 (diagnostic): least-squares exponent of ln y on ln x and its standard error. It answers does_not_change when |b| + k*se stays within the tolerance, changes when |b| - k*se is outside it, and undecided between or without a criterion; tolerance and multiple are rows. Cases: diffusivity along diameter (changes); a peak's width along integration time (does_not_change); a margin straddling the tolerance (undecided, with a nonzero standard error); no criterion (undecided).
(3) diffusive_regime_from_msd@v1 (diagnostic): the exponent over windows of consecutive lags against a tolerance on |alpha - 1|, the state over the last window, and diffusive_from, the lag from which every window is diffusive. Cases: an engine particle, ballistic then diffusive (from lag 4); a gel bead under a microscope, subdiffusive; no tolerance.
(4) steps_for_diffusive_displacement@v1 (estimate, engine units): run_time = (multiple*size)^2 / (2 d D) and steps = ceil(run_time / time_step). Cases: a colloid in Brownian dynamics; a tracer in molecular dynamics.
(5) timestep_max_from_diffusive_displacement@v1 (bound on time_step, engine units): (fraction*size)^2 / (2 d D), applying to any engine with a time_step row. Cases: as for (4).
Sources for (2) to (5): Wikipedia's Mean squared displacement (MSD = 2nDt), Anomalous diffusion (alpha = 1 normal) and Simple linear regression (slope and its variance over n - 2), each read on 2026-11-17 and cited with its section.
The estimate and the bound take engine units so they can bind to an engine's rows; an instrument in SI would need a version in SI units. The run-time skills take readings in one unit, as series_settled does. meta_agent/tests 301 OK, contracts/tests 116 OK.
